policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'out of thine eye' renders either preposition identically; no note bears on it.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'the beam out of thine own eye' follows English order and cannot report the Greek sequence.
Future indicative and aorist subjunctive after the negative purpose clause are both rendered 'lest haply they trample'; English does not distinguish.

ASV 'it shall be opened' is future passive, matching the future ἀνοιγήσεται rather than the present ἀνοίγεται, which the parallel presents 'receiveth'/'findeth' show ASV would have rendered as a present.
English requires a copula in 'what man is there of you' whether or not ἐστιν stands in the Greek; ASV does not mark it as supplied.

ASV renders a conditional clause, 'who, if his son shall ask him for a loaf', keeping the relative and adding 'if'; only ὃν ἐὰν αἰτήσῃ supplies the conditional particle, while the bare future relative αἰτήσει gives no 'if'.
ASV begins the verse 'or if he shall ask for a fish', rendering the disjunctive ἤ that the omission lacks.
ASV 'if he shall ask for a fish' is conditional; the conditional particle is present only in ἐὰν ἰχθὺν αἰτήσῃ, the plain future indicative giving no 'if'.
ἐάν and ἄν are interchangeable in the indefinite relative clause; ASV 'whatsoever ye would' renders either.
ASV text reads 'for wide is the gate', and the mapped textual note 'Some ancient authorities omit is the gate' assigns the omission to other authorities, so the ASV text includes ἡ πύλη.

The mapped note 'Many ancient authorities read How narrow is the gate' assigns τί to other authorities, so ASV's 'For narrow is the gate' renders ὅτι and excludes r02; between ὅτι and ὅτι δέ the English shows no adversative, but that is too slight to settle a connective at a sentence opening.
ASV opens 'Beware of false prophets' with no connective, but it regularly leaves δέ unrendered at a paragraph opening, so the English does not settle whether δέ stood in the text.
ASV 'grapes' renders the singular σταφυλήν, a cluster, as naturally as the plural; English number here does not report the Greek.
ASV renders both halves of the verse alike as 'bring forth', so it does not distinguish ποιεῖν from ἐνεγκεῖν at this point.
Presence or absence of the article with οὐρανοῖς is not reportable in ASV's 'in heaven'.
ASV 'shall be likened unto a wise man' is a third-person passive matching ὁμοιωθήσεται; ὁμοιώσω αὐτόν would give a first-person active 'I will liken him'.

ASV 'had finished these words' renders the simple and the compound verb alike; the perfective prefix leaves no trace in the English.
ASV 'not as their scribes' renders the possessive αὐτῶν, which the omission lacks.
